title: Resolve Offline Sync Anomaly and Implement Marketing Campaign State Synchronization
description: The TycoonX game is experiencing a critical data integrity issue. Players report that their 'Special Achievement' progress, tracked as a simple counter, is often incorrect or resets after they play offline and later reconnect. This suggests a conflict resolution problem in the offline sync mechanism. The first task is to diagnose and fix this data loss bug. Immediately following the fix, a new 'Marketing Campaign' feature needs its state to be made sync-aware. This new feature also includes a progress counter that will be subject to the same concurrency problems if not handled correctly. This multi-session task requires first fixing a complex bug in the synchronization layer and then applying the learned context to a new feature implementation.

project_spec.name: TycoonX: Franchise Empire Simulator
project_spec.description:
TycoonX: Franchise Empire Simulator is a mobile business-strategy game in which players build, acquire, and optimize a portfolio of real-world–inspired franchise chains (food, retail, fitness, etc.) while competing on a live leader board.  The title blends deep financial modeling with casual city-builder visuals, allowing users to negotiate leases, analyze foot-traffic heat maps, hire staff, and run targeted marketing campaigns.  A heavy business focus underpins every mechanic: cash-flow statements, supply-chain disruptions, customer-lifetime value, and KPI-based bonuses.

From an architectural standpoint, the game is implemented as a strict layered system.  Presentation (UI) drives cross-platform responsive scenes; a ViewModel layer exposes observable state for real-time dashboards; a domain-rich Business Logic layer encapsulates pricing algorithms, AI competitor behavior, and finance engines; a Data layer (Repositories + local SQL/NoSQL + remote REST/GraphQL adapters) provides offline-first persistence with conflict-resolution using CRDTs; and an Infrastructure layer plugs in third-party SDKs for camera store-front snapshots, crash analytics, biometric authentication, and geo-located push campaigns.  This separation makes it possible to iterate quickly on game mechanics that mimic real-world business processes while keeping each concern testable and replaceable.
dependencies: Cocos2d-x (C++) – cross-platform game engine with C bindings
SQLite / Realm – client-side persistent storage for offline_sync
libcurl + cJSON – REST/GraphQL networking for remote sync & analytics
Firebase SDK (C wrappers) – push_notifications, crash_reporting, analytics
OpenCV (mobile build) – camera_integration for storefront image capture
OpenSSL / Libsodium – secure communications and biometric_auth helpers
Google Play Services / Apple CoreLocation (C bridges) – location_services
RapidXML – lightweight XML parsing for configuration & save-file migration
libuv – cross-platform async I/O underpinning Observer and Adapter layers
